title: Mani Singh Refuses Surety and Offers His Life

blocks.text: The expected confrontation arrives as the scattered gathering fails to produce the money that Mughal officials demand. Bhai Mani Singh and other Singhs are seized, and the question of unpaid obligation is turned into an opportunity to pressure the Panth and its leaders.

Supporters in Lahore try to intervene, hoping to satisfy the authorities with guarantees or negotiated payment. Mani Singh prohibited all surety, however, refusing to let others rescue the situation through money when he sees that the real issue is no longer taxation but the testing of faith.

By rejecting both immediate rescue and deferred payment, Mani Singh effectively offers his own life in settlement. The page presents this not as fatalism, but as a conscious embrace of martyrdom over compromise.
